ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the lower left of the figure is an R–NH2 fragment, with a lone pair of electrons drawn on nitrogen; in the upper right is a protonated carbonyl-like structure, the carbon and oxygen are connected by a double bond, the oxygen carries a positive charge and is connected to hydrogen, and the carbon is also connected to two hydrogens. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason: after ignoring the arrows, only atoms and bonds are transcribed, giving two unconnected fragments: R–NH2 and H2C=OH+. In SMILES, R is represented by the wildcard atom '*', connected to nitrogen to give '*N'; the protonated carbonyl fragment is written as 'C=[OH+]'. The two unconnected fragments are connected with '.', therefore the SMILES is '*N.C=[OH+]'.

method.method_draft: Read the instruction to ignore arrows. From the image, transcribe only the atoms and bonds: R–NH2 is one disconnected fragment and H2C=OH+ is the other. Convert R to the wildcard atom '*' attached to N, giving '*N'. Convert the protonated carbonyl fragment to 'C=[OH+]'. Join the disconnected components with '.', yielding '*N.C=[OH+]'.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct atom-by-atom visual transcription is the most natural single route: read the drawn species while explicitly ignoring curved arrows, then encode the resulting disconnected fragments in SMILES.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the image to identify the non-arrow structural elements: a generic R-substituted amine shown as R–NH2 with a lone pair, and a separate protonated carbonyl/formaldehyde fragment where carbon is bonded to two hydrogens and double-bonded to O–H bearing a positive charge. Note that the curved arrows are reaction-mechanism annotations and are not part of the molecular graph.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to determine the required output format: a SMILES expression for the shown transition-state structure, explicitly excluding the curved arrows from the representation.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: represent an unspecified R attachment point as '*' bonded to nitrogen, write the amine fragment as '*N' with hydrogens implicit/understood from valence, represent protonated formaldehyde as 'C=[OH+]', and separate disconnected fragments with a dot.
